still_wrong.title: If you pause and then change an option, the preview stays on the 960 px poster. At DPR 2 that is softer than the frames, and the note says it is the video's frames
still_wrong.detail: In makePreview.start the fill draws a finished frame only when `!P.playing && (P.shown || o.autoplay)`. A restart from a paused state is not lazy and not autoplay, and P.shown is false at that point. So none of the new frames is ever shown. All of them are drawn and kept, but the user sees the poster until Play or a scrub. The poster is at most 960 px. At DPR 2 it is shown at 743 CSS px, which is 1486 device px: a 1.55x upscale, which is the softening vp-1 was about. The note reads 'Preview: the frames of the video itself, scaled to fit here and lightly compressed', but those frames are not what is on screen. It shows the same frame, so nothing jumps; it is only softer.
still_wrong.evidence: Probe p4: DPR 2, 1440 px, 1920x1080, 2 s per step. Playing: id 1, pw 1486, shown. Pause, then Ends -> Bounce. The new run (id 2) starts after 164 ms. After 6 s plus 2.5 s, shown is still false (until(shown) = -1), the poster is visible, the canvas is hidden, ready = 121/121 and pw = 1486. The poster's naturalWidth is 960 at 743 CSS px. Screenshot: work/xvv/test/vpv_cdp/shots/vpv-dpr2-paused-restart.png (softer than vpv-dpr2-canvas.png).
still_wrong.fix: When the run is not lazy, draw the frame at P.i once it is kept, even while paused. For example, in the fill: `if (!P.playing && (P.shown || o.autoplay || !q.lazy)) { P.drawn = -1; draw(P.i); }`. Reduced motion stays lazy and keeps the poster, as specified.

still_wrong.title: A screen-only change of sharpness (DPR changes, the window size does not) does not draw the frames again, although VIDEO-PREVIEW.md says it does
still_wrong.detail: Only the window 'resize' event calls pv.resize. Nothing listens for a change of devicePixelRatio, such as matchMedia('(resolution: Xdppx)'). Browser zoom changes the CSS size, so zoom is covered. Dragging the window from a 1x monitor to a retina one changes only the DPR, and browsers do not reliably fire 'resize' for that. The frames then stay at the 1x size and are shown upscaled 2x. The design note says: 'A bigger window (or a sharper screen) draws the frames again at the new size.'
still_wrong.evidence: Probe p4: dialog open at 1440 px, DPR 1, run id 3, pw 743. CDP setDeviceMetricsOverride to deviceScaleFactor 2 at the same width. After 1.2 s: id 3, pw 743, devicePixelRatio 2, 0 resize events. Caveat: in this emulation the matchMedia change event did not fire either, so this shows that the code path is missing. It does not prove what a real monitor move does.
still_wrong.fix: Add a re-armed listener: `const mq = () => { const m = matchMedia(`(resolution: ${devicePixelRatio}dppx)`); m.addEventListener('change', () => { onResize(); mq(); }, { once: true }); }`. Remove it on close together with the resize listener. Or remove '(or a sharper screen)' from the note.
